newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa seeks support in cargo logistics.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa seeks support in cargo logistics.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo has called on German forwarders to support its aim of becoming the leading supplier of air cargo logistics services.
Lufthansa Cargo (LCAG) chairman Wilhelm Althen said the airline and forwarders needed to work more closely together as partners in future to target and satisfy clients needs.
He made the call in a speech outlining the airline's new logistics strategy to some 130 German forwarders at a closed meeting with the German forwarders association BSL, an LCAG statement said.
"We intend turning Lufthansa Cargo into the leading logistics services supplier in the global air cargo market," Althen said.
Changes were necessary to keep the cargo airline competitive and together with forwarders, new avenues had to be pursued to meet customer needs, he added.
Lufthansa Cargo intended to offer customers an intercontinental network with a high-frequency schedule but needed partners to achieve this, Althen said.
"We aim to press ahead with Lufthansa Cargo's realignment together with you. Those of you willing to partner us are cordially welcome to join in," he stated.

LCAG Germany director, Joachim Steinbach, told forwarders: "I urge you to join in Lufthansa Cargo's new co-operation model. We will give priority to partners who join with us in improving customer benefits."

"If changes in co-operation between cargo carrier and agent are required to safeguard their competitiveness and improve their product and market image, then visions are entirely necessary," Dieter Alheit, BSL vice-chairman and airfreight committee chairman, told the meeting:
"But no visionary should forget that legionaries are essential to implement them," he added. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
